subtype: Approach: weighing danger against being laughed at [Thinking]
passage: Saturday. Pranav dared me to jump off the tall back wall by the water tank. Everyone stood in a half circle. I looked down and thought it through properly. If I land wrong, I could break a leg, and then no cricket, no school trip, and plaster for weeks. If I say no, they will make chicken noises for a day or two, and by Monday it will be a different joke. A broken leg is not forgotten by Monday. So I said, "No, thanks." My knees wobbled, but I walked home. At dinner I told Amma about the wall, and she hugged me and said she would speak to the watchman about it. Rehana

qa.q: What did Pranav dare Rehana to do?
qa.a: Pranav dared Rehana to jump off the tall back wall by the water tank.

qa.q: How did Rehana feel after saying no?
qa.a: Shaky but relieved, since Rehana's knees wobbled yet the walk home was safe. 😅

qa.q: What other approach could Rehana use the next time a dare comes, and why?
qa.a: Suggest a safer game or walk away with a friend, because it removes the danger without a long argument.

qa.q: How might the other children see Rehana's no?
qa.a: Some may tease for a day or two, but the jokes fade quickly, and others may quietly feel glad that someone said no.

grounding: Rehana, dared to jump from a high wall, weighs a broken leg against a few jokes and decides the jokes will pass sooner.

subtype: Approach: weighing danger against being laughed at [Thinking]
passage: The mud-brick wall behind the grain godown was taller than Hemant's father. Kunal and three other boys sat on top, legs swinging. "Jump, Hemant! Or are you a little goat?" Kunal called. Hemant looked down at the stony ground near the pump. He pictured his cousin Raju last winter, one leg in a white plaster for six weeks, missing every kabaddi match. Then he pictured Kunal bleating like a goat at school tomorrow. Maybe the day after too. By next week they'll be laughing at somebody's haircut, he thought. A plaster doesn't get bored and move on. "Bleat all you want," he said, and climbed down the side steps instead. Kunal bleated. Hemant bleated back, and two of the boys laughed with him.

qa.q: What did Hemant picture when he looked at the stony ground?
qa.a: He pictured his cousin Raju last winter, with one leg in a white plaster for six weeks, missing every kabaddi match.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling as he weighed the jump against the goat jokes?
qa.a: He was nervous and torn: afraid of an injury like Raju's, but also dreading being teased; comparing the two helped him feel steadier.

qa.q: What else could Hemant do if the teasing went on for days?
qa.a: He could stay with the boys who laughed with him and tell a teacher or his parents if it kept going, because teasing loses power without an audience.

qa.q: How might Kunal see Hemant's choice once Hemant bleats back?
qa.a: Kunal probably finds the dare less fun, because Hemant is joking along instead of looking hurt, and two boys are now laughing with Hemant, not at him.

grounding: Shows a boy weighing a possible broken leg against short-lived teasing and deciding the teasing will pass sooner.

subtype: Approach: weighing danger against being laughed at [Thinking]
passage: The old stone wall at the end of Calle Mayor dropped straight down to the car park. Emeka had already dared three boys, and all three had backed off. Now he pointed at Alejandro. "Your turn. Unless you're a chicken." Alejandro peered over the edge. Two storeys, maybe more. Okay. Think, he told himself. If I jump and land wrong, that's a cast, no football all spring, Mamá driving me to the hospital. If I don't jump, Emeka makes chicken noises until lunch. Maybe until Friday. Chicken noises stop. Bones take months. "Cluck away," Alejandro said. "I'm going to get churros." Emeka clucked twice, then jogged after him.

qa.q: How many boys had backed off Emeka's dare before Alejandro?
Why did Alejandro tell himself to think at the edge of the wall?
qa.a: He felt scared looking down at the two-storey drop and wanted to slow his fear down so he could compare a cast with a few chicken noises.

qa.q: Which other approach could Alejandro use if Emeka kept pushing?
qa.a: He could offer a safer contest, like a race to the churro stand, which keeps the fun and the competition without the drop.

qa.q: What might change for Emeka after Alejandro walks off?
qa.a: Emeka's dare loses its fun with no scared face to tease, and jogging after Alejandro suggests he would rather have company than keep daring.

grounding: Illustrates a boy imagining an injury against a moment of teasing and choosing to put up with the jokes.
